title: Who is on my team?
objective: Find a teammate before choosing whom to involve.
briefing: YOU have the puck in a sharing activity. Navy2 wears navy like you; Gold1 wears gold. The coach asks you to find your teammate. Navy attacks the +x end; gold attacks the -x end. The full rink is an orientation map for this small activity.

questions.prompt: Who is your teammate?
questions.explanation: Navy2 is on the same navy team as YOU. The labels also identify the teams.

questions.prompt: Which two things can you find here?
questions.explanation: Navy2 is your teammate and YOU have the puck. No goal has happened.

questions.prompt: Put this sharing routine in order.
questions.explanation: This is a suggested routine. Matching jerseys alone does not make a pass safe.

questions.prompt: Move YOU a little nearer Navy2 without standing on Navy2.
questions.explanation: This example shortens the distance while keeping separate space. Other clear starting spots could work.

questions.prompt: Imagine Gold1 steps between you and Navy2. What could you do?

options.text: Shoot the puck away without looking for Navy2

questions.explanation: A teammate can become covered. Look again or find clearer space. Sending the puck away before you look can give Gold1 a chance to get it.

questions.prompt: Tell a grown-up how you found your teammate.
questions.explanation: Mention navy, the Navy2 label or the team introduction. Pointing is fine.

title: A puck with nobody holding it
objective: Tell a loose puck from a carried puck.
briefing: The coach placed a puck in a quiet practice area. Nobody controls it yet. Navy2 waits beside the area. YOU are invited to collect it. Navy attacks the +x end; gold attacks the -x end. The full rink is an orientation map for this small activity.
cues: The puck is separate from both players.

questions.prompt: Who has the puck right now?
questions.explanation: The setup has no puck owner. It is between the players.

questions.prompt: What did the coach ask YOU to do?
questions.explanation: That is the instruction in the briefing.

questions.prompt: Arrange a gentle collection try.
questions.explanation: This is a suggested practice sequence; the picture does not measure skating or control.

questions.prompt: Show a place near the puck to finish your approach.
questions.explanation: The reference approaches without going far beyond the puck. Several nearby places may suit the activity.

questions.prompt: Imagine Navy2 reaches it first and controls it. Is it still loose?

options.text: Only until YOU skate over to it

questions.explanation: A puck is loose until a player controls it. Once Navy2 controls it in the stated event, it is not loose, even if another player is skating toward it.

questions.prompt: How could you tell the puck was waiting for someone?
questions.explanation: Point to the separate puck and notice that neither player controls it.

title: Room to carry
objective: Notice an occupied route and a roomier practice area.
briefing: YOU hold the puck. Gold1 is directly ahead. Navy2 waits off to one side. The coach invites you to explore the empty side away from Navy2. Navy attacks the +x end; gold attacks the -x end. The full rink is an orientation map for this small activity.
cues: Gold1 is ahead of YOUR facing direction.
Navy2 occupies one side of the practice area.
The opposite side has no player.

questions.prompt: Who is directly ahead of YOU?
questions.explanation: Gold1 is ahead in the direction YOU face.

questions.prompt: What is shown on the side away from Navy2?
questions.explanation: No player is placed on that side of the activity. Empty space does not guarantee an escape.

questions.prompt: Arrange this try at finding room.

options.text: Carry a short way and look again

questions.explanation: The routine invites another look when the situation changes.

questions.prompt: Move YOU into the empty practice space away from Navy2.
questions.explanation: This leaves the crowded line and the side Navy2 occupies. Other clear places may fit; a real route still needs checking.

questions.prompt: Imagine Navy2 moves into that empty space. What could you do?
questions.explanation: Notice the new player position instead of remembering one fixed spot.

questions.prompt: Point to one thing you checked before carrying.
questions.explanation: Gold1, Navy2 or the empty ice are relevant observations. Speaking or pointing is enough.

title: From the boards to the circle
objective: Use boards and faceoff circle to understand a practice instruction.
briefing: YOU are near the side boards. The coach names the nearby red ring a faceoff circle and asks you to return to its middle for the next turn. Navy2 waits outside the circle. Navy attacks the +x end; gold attacks the -x end. The full rink is an orientation map for this small activity.
cues: The named circle is centred near x=20.7, y=6.7.

questions.prompt: What does the coach call the nearby red ring?
questions.explanation: The briefing names this painted ring. It is a landmark in this practice.

questions.prompt: Where are YOU starting?
questions.explanation: YOU are close to the side boards and outside the painted circle.

questions.prompt: Arrange the return to our practice spot.

options.text: Check that the space is clear

questions.explanation: This is a suggested activity reset, not a faceoff rule or skating test.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward the middle of that faceoff circle.
questions.explanation: The reference is the stated practice spot. The coach could accept a nearby clear place; no tactical optimality is claimed.

questions.prompt: Imagine Navy2 stands in the middle first. What could you do?
questions.explanation: Give your partner room and follow the coach's next instruction. Skating into the spot anyway, or moving your partner out of it, takes the turn from them.

questions.prompt: Point to the boards, then point to the circle.
questions.explanation: Recognizing the two named areas is the aim. A point or spoken answer is enough.

title: Listen for the practice stop
objective: Recognize a stated practice stop signal.
briefing: In this practice only, one whistle means stop under control and listen. It has just sounded. YOU hold the puck; Navy2 uses a separate lane. This is not a match restart rule. Navy attacks the +x end; gold attacks the -x end. The full rink is an orientation map for this small activity.
cues: A practice stop signal was stated.

questions.prompt: What does this practice whistle mean?
questions.explanation: The briefing defines the signal for this activity.

questions.prompt: Which things help after that signal?
questions.explanation: Listening and awareness fit the instruction. These are suggested behaviours.

questions.prompt: Order this practice stop.
questions.explanation: The picture cannot measure stopping distance or technique.

questions.prompt: Is stopping the same as skating faster?

options.text: Yes, they both use your edges
Only when you are going fast

questions.explanation: Stopping and speeding up both use your edges, but they are different actions with different jobs. This practice signal asks for stopping under control.

questions.prompt: Now the coach invites a restart in your lane. What could you do?

options.text: Check the lane and begin gently
Start before the coach finishes talking
Assume every whistle has the same meaning

questions.explanation: Follow the new instruction. Waiting until the coach finishes and checking your own lane keeps the restart safe for both players. Another activity may use different signals.

questions.prompt: Tell a grown-up what you would listen for next.
questions.explanation: The next instruction or permission to begin is relevant. An adult can record spoken words.

title: Ready for a short pass
objective: Recognize the invited receiver and a partner-passing setup.
briefing: Navy2 holds the puck for a gentle partner pass. YOU wait at an angle. Gold1 stands outside this first activity and is not challenging. No pass has happened yet. Navy attacks the +x end; gold attacks the -x end. The full rink is an orientation map for this small activity.
cues: Gold1 is not challenging this try.

questions.prompt: Who starts with the puck?
questions.explanation: The puck is attached to Navy2.

questions.prompt: What is YOUR job in this activity?

options.text: Skate over and take the puck from Navy2
Wait with your back to Navy2

questions.explanation: The briefing identifies YOU as the receiver. Taking the puck from your partner, or turning away from them, would end the partner pass before it starts.

questions.prompt: Arrange a simple partner pass.

options.text: Get ready for the gentle pass

questions.explanation: This is a suggested progression. The eventual pass needs its own explicit movement; it is not shown yet.

questions.prompt: Move YOU a little nearer, leaving space between partners.
questions.explanation: This example shortens the distance. Other clear receiving places could work.

questions.prompt: Imagine Navy2 is not ready yet. What could you do?
questions.explanation: You can wait or communicate instead of forcing the activity.

questions.prompt: How could you show your partner you are ready?
questions.explanation: A clear look or simple call can help. Discuss a receiving target with the coach; no physical technique is graded.

title: My turn to defend the goal
objective: Recognize the goal-defending turn and nearby crease.
briefing: YOU have a short turn defending the navy goal at the -x end. The coach names the blue area in front of the net the crease. You are a skater taking a turn, not a permanent goalie. Gold1 has the puck; Navy2 takes the next turn. Navy attacks the +x end; gold attacks the -x end. The full rink is an orientation map for this small activity.
cues: YOU are assigned the navy goal at the -x end.
The blue area is named the crease.
Navy2 is next in the rotation.

questions.explanation: The briefing assigns YOU the navy goal at the -x end for this turn.

questions.prompt: What did the coach call the blue area by the net?
questions.explanation: The name is given in the briefing. This identifies an area, not a crease-entry rule.

questions.prompt: Arrange our goal-defending turns.
questions.explanation: This is the declared rotation; the coach controls the swap.

questions.prompt: Which facts belong to this activity?
questions.explanation: Gold1 owns the puck and Navy2 is next. The role is shared.

questions.prompt: Imagine Navy2 gains control of the puck. Who has it then?
questions.explanation: The answer follows the stated change of possession.

questions.prompt: How could you help Navy2 enjoy the next turn?
questions.explanation: Encouragement and room to try are useful answers. No goaltending technique is scored.

title: A teammate behind your shoulder
objective: Look beyond the forward direction to find a teammate.
briefing: YOU face the attacking end and hold the puck. Navy2 is behind your facing direction. Gold1 is ahead on the other side. The coach asks you to find Navy2 before deciding on a puck action. Navy attacks the +x end; gold attacks the -x end. The full rink is an orientation map for this small activity.
cues: Navy2 is behind that facing direction.
Finding Navy2 does not prove a pass is open.

options.text: Tell the coach where Navy2 is

questions.prompt: For a second try, move YOU away from the side with Navy2.

questions.prompt: Imagine Navy2 skates ahead of YOU. Should you keep pointing behind?
questions.explanation: Locate the teammate again when their position changes.

questions.prompt: Point to one thing you might miss by only watching the puck.

title: My partner has it now
objective: Recognize the new puck owner after a completed partner pass.
briefing: A gentle partner pass has finished. Navy2 controls the puck; YOU no longer do. This picture begins after reception and does not show the pass path. Leave Navy2 room while staying in the activity. Navy attacks the +x end; gold attacks the -x end. The full rink is an orientation map for this small activity.
cues: The earlier pass is stated, not animated.

title: A mistake and another try
objective: Respond kindly to a teammate error while noticing possession.
briefing: In a friendly keep-away activity, Navy2 missed a pass and Gold1 gained the puck. The picture starts after that change. Navy2 looks to YOU for encouragement; the coach invites everyone to keep trying. Navy attacks the +x end; gold attacks the -x end. The full rink is an orientation map for this small activity.
cues: Everyone is invited to try again.
